html:
Short answer: background music should be even and comfortable everywhere, never loud in one spot and silent in another. That means more, smaller speakers spread across zones, each with its own volume and music source, plus paging for announcements.

Plan by zone

  • Lobby, restaurant, bar, pool, gym, conference rooms, corridors and banking halls each become a zone.
  • Each zone gets its own volume and, where needed, its own music.
  • Paging can override music in selected zones.

Speakers

  • Ceiling speakers: discreet, even coverage indoors.
  • Wall and pendant speakers: for high or open ceilings.
  • Weather-resistant speakers: pool areas, terraces and gardens.

Sources and control

Streaming players, licensed music services and local sources feed a zone mixer or amplifier. Simple wall controls let staff adjust volume without touching the rack.

Events and conferences

Hotels hosting events also need portable or installed sound for speeches and functions. Design both together so they share equipment where sensible.

faqs.q: Can different areas play different music?
faqs.a: Yes. A multi-zone system lets each area choose its own source and volume.
Yes. Paging microphones or scheduled messages can automatically lower or mute music in selected zones.

faqs.q: Do I need a music licence in Kenya?
faqs.a: Businesses playing music to the public generally need licences from the relevant music rights bodies. Check your obligations before launch.
